rows.note: Use this all-purpose noun when a scratch means a minor injury rather than a mark on an object.

example.english: This is just a minor scratch, so don't worry.
example.traditional: 呢啲只係小傷，唔使擔心。
example.jyutping: ni1 di1 zi2 hai6 siu2 soeng1 m4 sai2 daam1 sam1

rows.note: Use this for a visible scratch mark on paint, furniture, a phone, or another surface.

example.english: There's a scratch on the table; I don't know who made it.
example.traditional: 張枱有條花痕，唔知邊個整花嘅。
example.jyutping: zoeng1 toi2 jau5 tiu4 faa1 han4 m4 zi1 bin1 go3 zing2 faa1 ge3

rows.note: This is the all-purpose choice for scratching an itch and, with a person or animal as subject, scratching with nails or claws.

example.english: The mosquitoes have bitten me all over, so I need to scratch.
example.traditional: 我俾蚊叮到成身都痕，要𢯎下先。
example.jyutping: ngo5 bei2 man1 ding1 dou3 seng4 san1 dou1 han4 jiu3 ngaau1 haa5 sin1

rows.note: Use this for leaving scratches on a surface or for saying that an object gets scratched.

example.english: My phone fell on the floor, and the case got a scratch.
example.traditional: 部手機跌咗落地，個殼刮花咗。
example.jyutping: bou6 sau2 gei1 dit3 zo2 lok6 dei6 go3 hok3 gwaat3 faa1 zo2

rows.note: Use this when rough fabric or another material pricks and irritates the skin rather than when someone deliberately scratches it.

example.english: This sweater feels rough against my skin and makes me want to scratch.
example.traditional: 件冷衫好拮肉，我着一陣就頂唔順。
example.jyutping: gin6 laang5 saam1 hou2 gat1 juk6 ngo5 zoek3 jat1 zan6 zau6 ding2 m4 seon6
